about: What the opening story reads that no record names yet. The address asks Congress for a President's own issue by the bill catalog's name for it, so only a name that reads as an action can follow "I ask Congress to": these are the first words that make one (OPUS-GOV's bill catalog, src/core2/data/legislature/bill-catalog.json). The town's lead story maps a public record's event kind to the newscast bank's kind of story.

sequence.about: The opening's sequence (owner, Oct 14, 2026, late): the President giving the address with the Vice President and key people behind, pointed out by name and office as the camera passes; then Congress (its leaders, your state's members); then your governor with a few leaders of your state legislature; then your family, if you have one; then home. Each part of the address plays over its stage, in the address's own order. Who the key people are is the owner's call (he clarifies tomorrow); until then they are picked from the offices and leadership records by rank, in the order listed. A stage with no one to point out still shows; a stage marked 'else' that finds no one hands its sentences to that stage, so a player with no family goes from the state's stage straight home. 'office' is a seat covering the player's town, by office kind; 'chamber' and 'post' a leadership post (data/research/legislature/chamber-leadership.json); 'household' the player's own household; 'most' caps how many are pointed out.

numbers.about: How the opening says its numbers: a figure to one decimal place ("4.2 percent"), and jobs in the thousands the payroll series counts and in millions past a million ("1.9 million"). Writing conventions, not estimates (AP Stylebook, numerals).

speechTitles.about: The address's own title, the topic the anchor's lead-in names ("We begin with {topic}."): the names the U.S. Constitution (Art. II, sec. 3) and the inauguration record give these addresses. A title, like an office's, not composed prose.

named.about: Who the address names, so the camera points them out on the sentence that does (owner, Oct 14, 2026: a person lit with no recorded reason is a defect). 'role' is the sequence rule that picked the figure; 'says' a word of the sentence's salutation; 'fact' a fact the sentence used, whose record is the figure's own. The player's household needs no sentence: the home is theirs.
